items.title: Why a status flip leaves no audit_log row
items.body:
The recovery branch runs `db.update(schema.monitor).set({ status: "active" })` directly in the workflows app. That is not a service verb, so `emitAudit` never runs and no `audit_log` row is written. ADR-008's evidence list and risk R5 name this asymmetry, together with the free-plan auto-pause; the fix they propose is system-actor audit rows, cheap because `system` is already in the Actor union.

- *emitAudit as a system actor*: that is the proposed fix, not today's code.
- *An audit trigger*: the database has no triggers for this.
- *Only apiKey and mcp rows*: `audit_log` records every actor type the services pass.

readMore.why: ADR-008 names the two pipeline paths that bypass the audit log.

items.title: Why the same quota hit gives 402 and 429
items.body:
The legacy v1 route counts monitors itself and, when `count >= limits.monitors`, throws `OpenStatusApiError({ code: "PAYMENT_REQUIRED", message: "Upgrade for more monitors" })`, a 402. The service verb raises a `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` ServiceError, and `toTRPCError` maps that to `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` (429); its comment argues a quota is not a permission problem. Risk R13 records the two public contracts disagreeing.

- *403 on both*: the adapter maps quota away from FORBIDDEN on purpose.
- *429 on REST and 402 on tRPC*: the two are the other way round.
- *409 on both*: CONFLICT is a separate ServiceError code.

items.title: Why a failed Tinybird send loses the probe result
items.body:
After a probe, the Go handler calls `h.TbClient.SendEvent(ctx, data, dataSourceName)`. If it returns an error, the handler logs 'failed to send event to tinybird' and continues. There is no buffer, spool or retry, and ADR-004 says probe results never touch SQL. So the row is simply gone, and with no loss metric nobody knows how often this happens; ADR-004 calls it the open wound of the telemetry plane.

- *Written to libSQL instead*: results never go to SQL.
- *Retried with backoff*: the error branch only logs.
- *Fails the Cloud Task*: the handler carries on, so the task is not failed by this.

excerpts.quote: log.Ctx(ctx).Error().Err(err).Msg("failed to send event to tinybird")

readMore.why: ADR-004 on the durability of the telemetry plane.

items.title: Why a foreign tag id gives FORBIDDEN, not NOT_FOUND
items.body:
`validateTagIds` selects tags whose id is in the list and whose `workspaceId` matches the caller's, then loops over the requested ids and throws a `ForbiddenError` with the message 'Tag N is not accessible.' (with the id in place of N) for any that did not come back. Other helpers in the same file, such as the monitor fetch-or-throw, raise `NotFoundError` for a foreign id. ADR-007 lists this 404-versus-403 mix as a known cleanup.

- *NotFoundError like the others*: this helper is the exception.
- *A ZodError*: the ids are well-formed numbers; the check is ownership.
- *Silently dropped*: any missing id throws.

excerpts.quote: throw new ForbiddenError(`Tag ${id} is not accessible.`);

items.title: Why a dashboard user passes requireScope untouched
items.body:
The function's first line is `if (actor.type !== "apiKey" && actor.type !== "mcp") return;`. A `user` actor (a dashboard session) never reaches the scope comparison. The docblock table says the same, and adds that member-role enforcement for users is a separate project; ADR-007 states the consequence plainly: any workspace member can currently do anything in the workspace.

- *A workspace-role check*: no role is read; that is the unbuilt project.
- *ForbiddenError for no scopes*: only key-based actors are compared against scopes.
- *A denied-attempt audit row*: denials are logged with `console.warn`, and there is no denial here anyway.

items.title: Concept: scopes, error translation and in-transaction audit
items.body:
ADR-007 says every caller is normalized into one `Actor` union and every verb throws domain errors that each transport translates at its own edge. ADR-008 adds an audit row inside the same transaction as each service mutation.

Read these files with the ADRs open:

- `packages/services/src/context.ts`: list the actor types.
- `packages/services/src/auth/require-scope.ts`: read the docblock table and then the code. Which actor types reach the scope comparison? What happens to the others? Note where the docblock says the call belongs, and why.
- `packages/services/src/monitor/internal.ts`: for each tenancy helper, write down what it does with an id from another workspace.
- `packages/api/src/service-adapter.ts`, `toTRPCError`: write down the TRPC code for each input type, including an error the function does not recognise, and which message the client sees.
- `apps/server/src/routes/v1/monitors/post.ts`: find the monitor-limit check and the error it throws.
- `packages/services/src/audit/emit.ts`: read `emitAudit`. When is `changedFields` null, when is it an empty array, and under which exact condition is the insert skipped? What happens if the entry is invalid?

excerpts.quote: Without a policy, validation gets skipped on the transport that "surely already checked,"

items.title: Why concurrent regional reports can both act
items.body:
Each request upserts its own region row, then reads the monitor with a plain `select`, decides from that snapshot, and later runs `db.update(...).set({ status })`. There are several awaits in between and no transaction around them. Two requests that arrive together can both read the old status and both take the transition branch, so the downstream dedupe is the only guard. The register suggests a compare-and-set update (`WHERE status = ?`) or per-monitor serialization.

- *One serializing transaction*: there is none in this handler.
- *A single worker*: nothing pins a monitor's reports to one process.
- *A compare-and-set*: that is the suggested fix, not the current code.

readMore.why: Risk R1 with its suggested test and fixes.

items.title: Why requireScope runs before the transaction opens
items.body:
The docblock gives the reason in two parts: a failed check should not open a transaction just to roll it back, and the check has no database dependency. `requireScope` only compares `ctx.actor.scopes` with the required scope, so running it first costs nothing and avoids pointless transaction work on a denied call.

- *A write lock on api_key*: the function reads no table.
- *Scopes read outside the tenant transaction*: scopes come from the actor already in `ctx`.
- *withTransaction swallowing errors*: nothing in the comment says so; the concern is wasted work.

excerpts.quote: A failed check shouldn't open a tx just to roll it back

items.title: Why soft-deleted monitors are not probed
items.body:
The cron selection filters on `periodicity`, `active = true` and not being in maintenance; it has no `deletedAt` condition. Soft-deleted monitors stay out only because the delete paths write `deletedAt` and `active: false` in the same update, as the service delete does. The guide calls this safe by convention, not by query, and suggests adding `isNull(deletedAt)` so a future writer cannot break it.

- *The maintenance filter*: it excludes monitors in a maintenance window, not deleted ones.
- *A view*: the query reads the `monitor` table directly.
- *The Go checker*: it probes whatever payloads cron sends, so the filtering happens upstream.

items.title: Why a no-diff update with metadata is still audited
items.body:
`emitAudit` computes `changedFields` with `diffTopLevel(before, after)` when both snapshots are present; identical snapshots give `[]`. The insert is skipped only when `changedFields` is an empty array AND `metadata` is undefined. The comment explains the exception: some changes live outside the row (for example a join table), so the metadata is the signal. Here the row is inserted with `changed_fields` as `[]`.

- *Skipped*: that is only for pure no-ops without metadata.
- *changed_fields NULL*: NULL means a snapshot was missing, as on creates and deletes.
- *Throws*: no rule requires an update to change a field.

items.title: Why an invalid audit entry rolls back the update
items.body:
`emitAudit` is called with the caller's transaction and starts with `auditEntrySchema.parse(entry)`. Nothing catches the `ZodError` it throws, so it propagates out of the transaction callback and the whole mutation rolls back. That is the meaning of fail-closed in ADR-008: if the record cannot be written, the change does not happen.

- *Commits and logs for retry*: best-effort audit is the first alternative ADR-008 rejected.
- *Written later by a queued job*: async audit was rejected too.
- *Caught inside emitAudit*: the function has no try/catch.

items.title: Start here: OpenStatus through its ADRs and its risk register
items.body:
OpenStatus is an open-source uptime monitor with public status pages. This checkout keeps the monorepo under `openstatus/`: `apps/checker` is a Go prober, `apps/workflows` runs cron fan-out and the `/updateStatus` state machine, `apps/server` serves the REST API, and `packages/services` holds the service verbs that every transport calls.

This quest reads four architecture decision records and the judgment files of the upskill course:

1. `fabledocs3/adr-003-go-checker-and-queue.md` and `adr-004-two-data-planes.md`: how probes run and where their results go.
2. `fabledocs3/adr-007-validation-and-errors.md` and `adr-008-fail-closed-audit.md`: how verbs validate, fail and record what they did.
3. `fabledocs/upskill/03-architecture-and-patterns/06-architecture-critique.md` and `fabledocs/upskill/09-reference/risk-register.md`.

Each ADR ends with an Evidence list and the register marks every row confirmed or hypothesis. Open the cited lines before you trust a sentence: one ADR evidence path in this checkout points at a file that is not there.

excerpts.quote: Living document. Confidence: **confirmed** = behavior read directly in code

items.title: Concept: evidence, verdict and the shared pipeline
items.body:
Probes run in many regions. OpenStatus separates **evidence** (one `monitor_status` row per region) from the **verdict** (the monitor's global `status`). Read the `/updateStatus` handler in `apps/workflows/src/checker/index.ts` from the top:

- How is `numberOfRegions` computed, and how is `affectedRegionCount` counted?
- Find the condition that decides a flip. Work it through for monitors with 1, 2, 4 and 5 regions and different counts of failing regions.
- Mark every `await` between reading `monitor.status` and writing it. Then picture two regions' requests running at the same time and follow both.
- Note which function performs each write in the handler.

Then look at the two edges of the pipeline. In `apps/checker/handlers/checker.go`, find where a probe result is sent to Tinybird and read the error branch. In `apps/workflows/src/cron/checker.ts`, read the query that selects monitors to probe and list its filters, then read what happens right after it when the rows are parsed. Finally read how the service-layer delete in `packages/services/src/monitor/delete.ts` changes a monitor.

readMore.why: Cron selection of monitors to probe.

items.title: Why two of four regions are enough to flip
items.body:
The handler counts the regions whose latest `monitor_status` matches the reported status, then flips only if `affectedRegionCount >= numberOfRegions / 2 || numberOfRegions === 1`. For 4 regions the threshold is 2, and `2 >= 2` is true, so an even split flips the status. For 5 regions it would take 3, since 2 is less than 2.5.

- *A strict majority*: the comparison is `>=` half, so a tie is enough.
- *Every region must agree*: the test is a share, not unanimity.
- *Any single region*: that applies only to a monitor with exactly one region.

items.title: Why an unknown error reaches tRPC as a generic 500
items.body:
`toTRPCError` checks, in order: an existing `TRPCError` (rethrown), a `ZodError` (BAD_REQUEST, 'Invalid input'), and each `ServiceError` code. A plain `Error` matches none, so it reaches the final throw: `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` with the fixed message 'Internal server error' and the original error on `cause`. The comment explains why: raw messages can leak database strings and SDK internals.

- *The original SQLITE_BUSY text*: the message is replaced; only `cause` keeps it.
- *BAD_REQUEST 'Invalid input'*: that branch is for ZodError.
- *CONFLICT*: only a ServiceError with code CONFLICT maps there.

excerpts.quote: code: "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", message: "Internal server error", cause: err,
